body_result.note: R6 finally proves the real flight-front and preserves the accepted FBX orientation. Do not rotate or replace the body.

visual_blockers: Muzzle reads as a small cluster of round white eggs with soft halos; it lacks a decisive seven-port shotgun pressure silhouette and remains materially smaller than the body identity demands.

Flight is three or four detached blurry puffs behind the body. It does not make continuous body contact, does not taper into a wake, and reads like repeated sprites rather than propulsion from seven chambers.
Impact remains a small irregular blob with curved bright strips; its contact, peak and fragment fan do not establish a broad seven-chamber hit at gameplay scale.
The comparison frame shows the effect stages as tiny isolated marks around a large body, so the complete suite still falls below the user commercial floor despite the now-good body proof.

preserve: FBX, Muzzle, Projectile, Impact and suite GUIDs
body orientation, hierarchy and R5/R6 evidence
r7_constraints.muzzle: Build one 1.6x to 2.0x larger asymmetric seven-port pressure burst. The seven hot cores must sit inside one coherent warm outer mass; use short varied wedges/fragments only as accents. Avoid equal round blobs, rings, bars, needles and line stars.
r7_constraints.flight: Replace detached puff beads with one continuous tapered rear-contact wake at least 0.75 body lengths. It must visibly originate from the rear chamber plane, use an overlapping hot-core/warm-outer/soot hierarchy, and break into only two or three small terminal embers.
r7_constraints.impact: Create a 1.8x to 2.3x larger broad contact burst with seven unequal hot punches embedded in one asymmetrical pressure cloud, a short forward-and-side fragment fan and readable soot decay. Remove curved strip/ring impressions.
r7_constraints.capture: Preserve the +Z body proofs and add M/F/I gameplay-scale comparison panels where each effect occupies enough screen area to judge its shape; rerun all original 1024x768 timing frames and 30-cycle residue.

forbidden: white bars, needles or line stars
